old: Its name was carried west by 13th-century Florentine merchants trading with an Armenian kingdom.
Before it wore an English coat, it wore an Italian and French one — carpita and carpite.
Trace it back far enough and you land on Armenian կապերտ (kapert), the word's oldest known form.
clues: This household furnishing takes its name from Armenian; Florentines brought the word into Europe in the 13th century.
A thick woven or tufted covering for a floor, often fitted wall to wall, unlike a rug, which is a loose piece covering only part of the room.
Celebrities walk the red one at premieres, Aladdin soars over Agrabah on a magic one, and being called on it means getting a scolding.
